slides.texte_overlay:
Things that make you quietly
confident at work
Speak once in every meeting. Not ten times, once, with something useful. "Can I add one thing?" People remember the guy who talks rarely and always adds value.
Keep a short list of your wins. Every Friday, write what you finished. When review time comes, you'll calmly know your worth instead of trying to remember it on the spot.
Ask for feedback before anyone gives it. "What's one thing I could do better on this?" Asking first shows you're secure enough to hear it, and it turns your boss into an ally.
Learn things outside your job. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science. It makes me calmer in meetings, because I've always got a wider view than the problem in front of me.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It makes me calmer in meetings, because I always have a wider view than the problem in front of me.

slides.texte_overlay: Leave on time most days. Working late every night doesn't look dedicated, it looks disorganised. Finish, close the laptop, go. Quiet confidence includes knowing your limits.
Dress one level above the office. A clean shirt, decent shoes. You don't need a suit. Looking put together on an ordinary Wednesday tells people you take yourself seriously.
Don't fight for credit. Do excellent work and let it speak. The people who matter notice. Chasing credit loudly makes you look insecure, even when you deserve it.
